# Kaṇaverajātaka (Ja 318)

**ID:** Ja 318
**Section:** Jātaka (ja)
**Collection:** Suttas-Late-1
**Title (Pali):** Kaṇaverajātaka
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/s0513m.mul3.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

Suspicious that her unfaithfulness might lead her to betray him as she had others, the robber later lured her into a thicket of *kaṇavera* bushes, choked her unconscious, stole her jewelry, and escaped; despite her attempts to woo him back, he refused to return [Appleton 2010; Cowell 1897]. Buddhist commentators and modern scholars frequently cite the narrative as a rare depiction of the Bodhisatta committing serious wrongdoing, reflecting the doctrinal idea that unenlightened Bodhisattas retain mortal flaws due to astrological or karmic circumstances [Narada 2008; Appleton 2010; Chen 2015].

DharmaNexus records Pali-internal text reuse with the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (eight matches totaling 718 characters), while showing no machine matches meeting the score threshold in non-Pali corpora [DharmaNexus].
